urls.reviewedSupport: Owner and optional limiter are stored; calculateSteering delegates when enabled and clears the supplied output when disabled.
Seek uses target-minus-owner position, normalises and scales to maximum linear acceleration, and clears angular acceleration.
Linear and angular fields and setZero/add/scl/mulAdd affect both channels; the class contains no body integration.
Flee extends Seek, reverses the position subtraction, scales the normalised direction to the allowed acceleration and clears angular output; this method has no fade.
MatchVelocity uses target-minus-owner linear velocity divided by timeToTarget, limits linear acceleration and clears angular output without reading position.
Relative-velocity time, scalar distance-minus-relative-speed filtering, earliest candidate retention, current-offset fallback and normalised maximum-acceleration output match the explanation.
Immediate close neighbours precede nearest-approach prediction. Future threats are filtered by twice owner radius; heading cases select a lateral sign, with the stated crossing-speed condition.
Configured rays are refreshed, nearest hit is selected, hit normal offsets the target by body radius plus margin, and no hit clears output. The class comments discuss corner traps.
The raw file matches the raycast implementation and documents adaptive fan angles and temporary winner rays as recovery proposals rather than code implemented in the class.
Weighted child output accumulation and linear limiting are present; documentation explicitly says weights need not total one.
Priority uses a squared-magnitude epsilon test, supports blended groups, and returns the last small output if no child clears the threshold.
The no-air-resistance treatment gives constant horizontal velocity and the constant-gravity height quadratic; time is shared between the axes.
FixedUpdate applies the current/previous-position Verlet-style update, impulse times dt and gravity times dt squared, points along movement, clears impulse and destroys below a height cutoff.
The stationary-target fixed-speed derivation solves horizontal time, substitutes it into height and obtains low and high firing angles.
The stationary solver checks the discriminant, forms two angles, deduplicates equal angles and constructs fixed-speed velocity vectors; a moving-target overload follows.
Bisection uses midpoint evaluation and sign-based interval retention; the manual requires a zero crossing for bracketing and separates accuracy, iteration-budget and error stops.
Jump derives flight time and planar velocity, checks speed feasibility, requires both takeoff position and velocity tolerances, invokes a takeoff callback and otherwise delegates to MatchVelocity.
The entity computes steering, leaves a documented motor-filter insertion point, applies force and torque or velocity-facing, and records the timing limitation of speed caps.
Vehicle obtains steering force, divides by mass, integrates and caps velocity, moves position, and optionally updates orientation from raw or smoothed velocity without smoothing position.
SeekBehavior computes a maximum-speed Vector3 desired velocity and returns its difference from current velocity.
The controller separates horizontal and vertical velocity, processes gravity and jumping, recombines before move_and_slide, and fixes Vector3.UP in the grounded mesh basis.
Both smoothed and straight path-steering calculations clear the vertical direction component.
movePosition moves along the navigation surface, merges the corridor and retrieves polygon height for the resulting position; rendered yaw is not prescribed here.
KinematicArrive uses a strict squared-radius test, otherwise divides offset by timeToTarget and clips speed; it returns output without advancing position.
The header explicitly distinguishes immediately adopted kinematic velocity from acceleration-based dynamic motion and declares arrival time and radius.
The maintainer labels the repository historical and states that it did not keep up with algorithm corrections or the third edition.
Translation runs at equality or beyond targetRadius, normalises direction and uses maxSpeed as per-iteration displacement without elapsed-time scaling or taper.
Arrive returns zero output at or below arrivalTolerance; outside it, desired velocity is tapered and acceleration is bounded, without setting owner velocity.
Two uniform draws are subtracted; separate coroutines assign absolute Euler rotation and translate along forward with no elapsed-time multiplier.
Formation delegates assignment, updates slot count, obtains relative slots, transforms them by anchor, applies drift, writes member target locations and calls an optional moderator.
The moderator exposes a per-frame anchor update hook and computes drift from averaged occupied slot positions and orientations.

usage.source: No cumulative model token counter is exposed to this worker; command-output token estimates are not model token usage.
usage.scope: This independent factual critic, including source checks, cited-source inspection, twenty initial path-alias probes and twenty corrected canonical serial probes.

additionalProbes.reason: The first serial driver resolved the supplied /var probe path to the equivalent /private/var spelling. During report validation this literal-path deviation was noticed, disclosed and corrected by rerunning all twenty with exactly the supplied /var command spelling. These earlier successful probes are preserved as audit history and are not substituted for the canonical results.

projection: Public projection omits repeated console logs, copied catalog definitions and absolute private workspace paths. The original receipt hash binds the retained private report.
